explanation: I found no Mathlib declaration that states this result. The library's proof derives it from its own lemma `norm_of_sum_sq_eq_sum_norm_sq_iff`, which is not part of Mathlib. The closest Mathlib results are `Complex.norm_add_eq_iff` (in Mathlib/Analysis/Complex/Arg.lean: ‖x+y‖ = ‖x‖+‖y‖ ↔ x = 0 ∨ y = 0 ∨ x.arg = y.arg) and `norm_add_eq_iff_real` (in the inner-product-space file). Turning either into this statement would take real work: apply it to x = α₁², y = α₂², then convert a condition on arguments of squares into α₁.re·α₂.im = α₂.re·α₁.im. That is more than a one- or two-line derivation. I also grepped for re/im cross-product identities and for norm-of-sum equality lemmas under Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Complex and across Mathlib, and found nothing closer.
